dialogues.title: Opening a Bank Account
dialogues.situation: You go to a bank to open your first account and get a debit card.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Hello. What brings you in today?
lines.note: standard bank greeting

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I would like to open an account.
lines.note: 통장 = bankbook/account

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Did you bring your ID?
lines.note: 신분증 = ID card

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, here is my alien registration card.
lines.note: 외국인등록증 = ARC, the foreigner ID

lines.ko: 여기 신청서에 성함하고 연락처 적어 주세요.
lines.romanization: yeogi sincheongseoe seonghamhago yeollakcheo jeogeo juseyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Please write your name and phone number on this form here.
lines.note: 성함 = honorific for name

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Can I get a debit card with it too?
lines.note: 체크카드 = debit card

lines.ko: 네, 가능해요. 비밀번호 네 자리 눌러 주세요.
lines.romanization: ne, ganeunghaeyo. bimilbeonho ne jari nulleo juseyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that is possible. Please enter a four-digit PIN.
lines.note: 비밀번호 = password/PIN

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I would also like to sign up for internet banking.

lines.ko: 그럼 휴대폰으로 본인 인증 한번 할게요.
lines.romanization: geureom hyudaeponeuro bonin injeung hanbeon halgeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then let me verify your identity with your phone.
lines.note: 본인 인증 = identity verification

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: When does the card come out?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I will issue it right now. One moment please.
lines.note: 발급 = issue

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Okay, thank you.

dialogues.tip: Bring your 외국인등록증 (ARC) and a Korean phone number, since banks verify your identity by phone. New foreign accounts often start with a low daily transfer limit for fraud protection.

dialogues.title: Asking About a Transfer
dialogues.situation: You go to the bank counter to send money and ask about the transfer limit and fee.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello. I came to make a transfer.
lines.note: 계좌이체 = bank transfer

lines.ko: 네, 받는 분 계좌번호 알고 계세요?
lines.romanization: ne, banneun bun gyejwabeonho algo gyeseyo?
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, do you know the recipient's account number?
lines.note: 받는 분 = the person receiving

lines.ko: 네, 여기 적어 왔어요. 백만 원 보내고 싶어요.
lines.romanization: ne, yeogi jeogeo wasseoyo. baengman won bonaego sipeoyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, I wrote it down here. I want to send one million won.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Have you by any chance checked your transfer limit?
lines.note: 이체 한도 = transfer limit

lines.ko: 한도가 얼마예요? 오늘 다 보낼 수 있어요?
lines.romanization: handoga eolmayeyo? oneul da bonael su isseoyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What is the limit? Can I send it all today?

lines.ko: 하루 한도가 백만 원이라서 딱 돼요.
lines.romanization: haru handoga baengman woniraseo ttak dwaeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Your daily limit is one million won, so it works exactly.
lines.note: -라서 = because (giving a reason)

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How much is the fee?
lines.note: 수수료 = fee

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: If it is the same bank, it is free.
lines.note: -(으)면 = if

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What if it is a different bank?

lines.ko: 오백 원 붙어요. 비밀번호 눌러 주세요.
lines.romanization: obaek won buteoyo. bimilbeonho nulleo juseyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: There is a 500 won charge. Please enter your PIN.
lines.note: 붙다 = to be added on

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Did it go through? Will I get a confirmation text?

lines.ko: 네, 이체 완료됐어요. 문자 갈 거예요.
lines.romanization: ne, iche wallyodwaesseoyo. munja gal geoyeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, the transfer is complete. A text will be sent.
lines.note: 완료 = completion

dialogues.tip: If you hit your daily 이체 한도, you can raise it in the bank app or in person, though raising it usually needs extra verification. Transfers within the same bank are free, while inter-bank transfers add a small fee.

dialogues.title: Move-in Report at the Community Center
dialogues.situation: You go to the 주민센터 to report a change of address and pick up a residence document.

lines.ko: 안녕하세요. 번호표 뽑고 잠시만 기다려 주세요.
lines.romanization: annyeonghaseyo. beonhopyo ppopgo jamsiman gidaryeo juseyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Hello. Please take a number and wait a moment.
lines.note: 번호표 = number ticket

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Okay. I came to file a move-in report.
lines.note: 전입신고 = move-in/address report

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: What is your new address?
lines.note: polite way to ask for info

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I moved to Yeoksam-dong, Gangnam-gu.
lines.note: -(으)로 = marks destination

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Could you show me your ID and lease contract?
lines.note: 계약서 = contract

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Here you go. How many days until it is processed?
lines.note: 처리되다 = to be processed

lines.ko: 오늘 바로 처리돼요. 여기 서명해 주세요.
lines.romanization: oneul baro cheoridwaeyo. yeogi seomyeonghae juseyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It is processed today right away. Please sign here.
lines.note: 서명 = signature

lines.ko: 그리고 주민등록등본도 한 통 떼고 싶어요.
lines.romanization: geurigo jumindeungnokdeungbondo han tong ttego sipeoyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: And I would also like to get one copy of a residence certificate.
lines.note: 등본 한 통 떼다 = print one copy of a certificate

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: The fee is 400 won—would you like to pay by card?
lines.note: -(으)ㄴ데 = and/so (background)

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: By any chance, can I get the document in English too?
lines.note: -(으)로 된 = made in/written in

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: An English document has to be requested separately.
lines.note: -아/어야 되다 = have to

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I see. Then just the certificate please. Thank you.

dialogues.tip: You must report a move within 14 days. Bring your ID and lease, and you can print a 주민등록등본 (residence certificate) at the same visit. Foreign residents may instead report at an immigration office, so check which applies to your visa.

dialogues.title: Viewing a One-Room with a Real Estate Agent
dialogues.situation: You found a 원룸 listing online and meet a 부동산 agent to view a monthly-rent (월세) studio in person.

lines.ko: 안녕하세요. 인터넷에서 보고 연락드렸는데요, 그 원룸 보러 왔어요.
lines.romanization: annyeonghaseyo. inteoneseseo bogo yeollakdeuryeonneundeyo, geu wollum boreo wasseoyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello. I called after seeing it online — I came to view that one-room.
lines.note: 보고 연락드렸는데요 = a polite, natural way to say 'I contacted you after seeing it'; 드리다 humbles the verb

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Ah, yes. Shall we go right up and take a look? It's on the 4th floor.
lines.note: 보실까요 = 'shall we look?'; -(으)ㄹ까요 suggests doing something together

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What are the deposit and the monthly rent?
lines.note: 어떻게 돼요 = the standard way to ask 'what is it / how much is it' for set figures

lines.ko: 보증금 천만 원에 월세 오십이에요. 관리비는 따로 칠만 원이고요.
lines.romanization: bojeunggeum cheonman wone wolse osibieyo. gwallibineun ttaro chilman wonigoyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's a ten-million-won deposit with 500,000 a month. The maintenance fee is 70,000 separately.
lines.note: 보증금 천에 월세 오십 = how Koreans say rent: deposit 'X' with monthly 'Y'; 만 원 is dropped in speech

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What's included in the maintenance fee? Is water included too?
lines.note: 포함되다 = to be included; 수도세 = water bill

lines.ko: 수도세랑 인터넷은 포함이고, 전기세랑 가스비는 따로 내셔야 돼요.
lines.romanization: sudoserang inteoneseun pohamigo, jeongiserang gaseubineun ttaro naesyeoya dwaeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Water and internet are included, but you have to pay electricity and gas separately.
lines.note: -셔야 돼요 = honorific of -아/어야 돼요 (have to); 따로 = separately

lines.ko: 옵션은 뭐가 있어요? 세탁기랑 에어컨 있어요?
lines.romanization: opsyeoneun mwoga isseoyo? setakgirang eeokeon isseoyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What options does it come with? Is there a washing machine and air conditioner?
lines.note: 옵션 = built-in appliances/furnishings that come with the unit

lines.ko: 풀옵션이에요. 냉장고, 세탁기, 에어컨, 인덕션 다 있어요.
lines.romanization: puropsyeonieyo. naengjanggo, setakgi, eeokeon, indeoksyeon da isseoyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's fully furnished. Fridge, washing machine, AC, and an induction stove — it has everything.
lines.note: 풀옵션 = 'full option', the common term for a fully equipped studio

lines.ko: 방이 좀 어두운 것 같은데, 햇빛은 잘 들어와요?
lines.romanization: bangi jom eoduun geot gateunde, haetbicheun jal deureowayo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: The room seems a bit dark — does it get good sunlight?
lines.note: 햇빛이 들어오다 = (sun)light comes in; 채광 is the noun for natural lighting

lines.ko: 남향이라서 낮에는 햇빛 잘 들어와요. 곰팡이 걱정은 없으실 거예요.
lines.romanization: namhyangiraseo najeneun haetbit jal deureowayo. gompangi geokjeongeun eopseusil geoyeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It faces south, so it gets good light during the day. You won't have to worry about mold.
lines.note: 남향 = south-facing, a big selling point; 곰팡이 = mold, a real concern in cheap 원룸

lines.ko: 마음에 들어요. 다음 달 초에 입주 가능해요?
lines.romanization: maeume deureoyo. daeum dal choe ipju ganeunghaeyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I like it. Can I move in early next month?
lines.note: 입주 = moving in; 다음 달 초 = early next month

lines.ko: 네, 가능해요. 계약하시려면 가계약금 먼저 넣으시면 돼요.
lines.romanization: ne, ganeunghaeyo. gyeyakasiryeomyeon gagyeyakgeum meonjeo neoeusimyeon dwaeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that's possible. If you want to sign, you just put down a holding deposit first.
lines.note: 가계약금 = a small holding deposit to reserve the unit before the full contract

dialogues.tip: Rent is quoted as '보증금 / 월세' (deposit / monthly), and 관리비 (maintenance fee) is almost always extra — always ask what it covers. Check 옵션 (appliances), 채광/방향 (light & direction), and look for 곰팡이 (mold). Never wire a 가계약금 until you've confirmed the listed owner matches the property register (등기부등본).

dialogues.title: Calling the Landlord About a Broken Boiler and Leak
dialogues.situation: Your hot water stopped working and there's a water leak under the sink, so you call your 집주인 to ask for repairs.

lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.en: Hello, sir. This is the tenant in unit 402.
lines.note: 사장님 = a common, respectful way tenants address a landlord; 여보세요 = 'hello' on the phone

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: Yes, is something the matter?
lines.note: 무슨 일 있으세요 = 'is something wrong?', a natural phone opener

lines.ko: 어제부터 보일러가 고장 나서 따뜻한 물이 안 나와요.
lines.romanization: eojebuteo boilleoga gojang naseo ttatteutan muri an nawayo.
lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.en: The boiler has been broken since yesterday, so no hot water comes out.
lines.note: 고장 나다 = to break down; 어제부터 ... 안 나와요 = '(it) hasn't come out since yesterday'

lines.ko: 아이고, 추운데. 온수만 안 나와요, 아니면 난방도 안 돼요?
lines.romanization: aigo, chuunde. onsuman an nawayo, animyeon nanbangdo an dwaeyo?
lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: Oh no, and it's cold out. Is it only the hot water, or is the heating out too?
lines.note: 온수 = hot water (formal); 난방 = heating — boilers in Korea handle both

lines.ko: 난방도 안 돼요. 그리고 싱크대 밑에서 물이 새요.
lines.romanization: nanbangdo an dwaeyo. geurigo singkeudae miteseo muri saeyo.
lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.en: The heating is out too. And water is leaking under the sink.
lines.note: 물이 새다 = to leak; 싱크대 밑 = under the sink

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: A leak on top of that? Has a lot of water pooled on the floor?
lines.note: 누수 = water leakage (the noun you'll see on repair bills); 물이 고이다 = water pools up

lines.ko: 네, 수건으로 막아 놨는데 계속 새요. 빨리 좀 고쳐 주셨으면 좋겠어요.
lines.romanization: ne, sugeoneuro maga nwanneunde gyesok saeyo. ppalli jom gochyeo jusyeosseumyeon jokesseoyo.
lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.en: Yes, I blocked it with a towel but it keeps leaking. I'd really appreciate it if you could fix it soon.
lines.note: 고쳐 주셨으면 좋겠어요 = a polite, indirect request: 'I'd be grateful if you'd fix it'

lines.ko: 알겠어요. 오늘 바로 기사님 보낼게요. 몇 시에 집에 계세요?
lines.romanization: algesseoyo. oneul baro gisanim bonaelgeyo. myeot sie jibe gyeseyo?
lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: Understood. I'll send a technician right away today. What time will you be home?
lines.note: 기사님 = repair technician (honorific); 보낼게요 = 'I'll send', the landlord's promise

lines.ko: 저녁 7시 이후에 집에 있어요. 그 전엔 회사라서요.
lines.romanization: jeonyeok 7si ihue jibe isseoyo. geu jeonen hoesaraseoyo.
lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.en: I'm home after 7 p.m. Before that I'm at work.
lines.note: -라서요 = trailing 'because...', softens the reason

lines.ko: 그럼 7시 반쯤 기사님이 연락드릴 거예요. 수리비는 제가 낼게요.
lines.romanization: geureom 7si banjjeum gisanimi yeollakdeuril geoyeyo. suribineun jega naelgeyo.
lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: Then the technician will contact you around 7:30. I'll cover the repair cost.
lines.note: 수리비 = repair fee; landlords pay for repairs to fixtures like the boiler

lines.ko: 감사합니다. 혹시 못 고치면 보일러 교체도 가능할까요?
lines.romanization: gamsahamnida. hoksi mot gochimyeon boilleo gyochedo ganeunghalkkayo?
lines.speaker: 세입자
lines.en: Thank you. If it can't be fixed, would replacing the boiler be possible too?
lines.note: 교체 = replacement; -(으)ㄹ까요 here softly checks possibility

lines.ko: 기사님이 보고 판단할 거예요. 너무 걱정 마세요.
lines.romanization: gisanimi bogo pandanhal geoyeyo. neomu geokjeong maseyo.
lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: The technician will decide after looking. Don't worry too much.
lines.note: 걱정 마세요 = 'don't worry', a reassuring set phrase

dialogues.tip: Repairs to fixed installations — 보일러 (boiler), 누수 (leaks), 변기 (toilet) — are normally the landlord's (집주인) responsibility, so report them fast by phone. Take photos and a quick video as evidence, and confirm who pays (수리비) before the 기사님 (technician) arrives. Address your landlord as 사장님 or 사모님 to keep it polite.

dialogues.title: Buying Cold Medicine at the Pharmacy
dialogues.situation: You catch a cold and go to a 약국 to describe your symptoms and buy over-the-counter medicine.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Welcome. What's bothering you?
lines.note: 어디가 안 좋으세요 = a softer, common way to ask what's wrong

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I've felt a cold coming on since yesterday.
lines.note: 감기 기운 = signs/onset of a cold, a very natural phrase

lines.ko: 증상이 어떻게 되세요? 콧물이나 기침 있으세요?
lines.romanization: jeungsangi eotteoke doeseyo? konmurina gichim isseuseyo?
lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: What are your symptoms? Do you have a runny nose or a cough?
lines.note: 증상 = symptom; ~이나 lists options

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I have a runny nose and my throat feels a bit scratchy.
lines.note: 따끔거리다 = to feel prickly/scratchy

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: What about a fever? Do you have one too?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: No fever, but I feel a bit chilly and shivery.
lines.note: 으슬으슬하다 = the chilly, shivery feeling of a cold

lines.ko: 그럼 종합감기약 드릴게요. 졸린 성분이 들어 있어요.
lines.romanization: geureom jonghapgamgiyak deurilgeyo. jollin seongbuni deureo isseoyo.
lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Then I'll give you a combination cold medicine. It has a drowsy ingredient in it.
lines.note: 종합감기약 = all-in-one cold medicine

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How many times a day do I take it?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Take it three times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
lines.note: 식후 30분 = 30 minutes after eating, the standard dosing line

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Is it okay to drive after taking this?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: It may make you drowsy, so avoid driving.
lines.note: ~(으)니까 = because/so; gives a reason before advice

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Got it. How much is it?

dialogues.tip: For colds, fevers, and minor pain you can buy medicine straight from a 약국 without a prescription. Just describe your 증상 (symptoms) clearly. For most antibiotics you'll need a doctor's prescription (처방전) first.

dialogues.title: Registering at a Clinic Front Desk
dialogues.situation: You arrive at a 의원 (clinic) for the first time and check in at the front desk before seeing the doctor.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Hello. Let me help you check in. Is this your first visit?
lines.note: 접수 = registration/check-in; 처음 오셨어요 asks if you're a new patient

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, it's my first time.

lines.ko: 그럼 이 문진표 좀 작성해 주세요. 신분증 있으세요?
lines.romanization: geureom i munjinpyo jom jakseonghae juseyo. sinbunjeung isseuseyo?
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then please fill out this form. Do you have an ID?
lines.note: 문진표 작성하다 = to fill out a medical questionnaire; 신분증 = ID card

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Is an Alien Registration Card okay too?
lines.note: 외국인등록증 = ARC, the ID foreigners carry in Korea

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that's fine. Do you have health insurance?
lines.note: 건강보험 = national health insurance

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, I have insurance through my job.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: What are you here to see the doctor about?
lines.note: 어디가 불편하세요 = a polite, standard way to ask your reason for visiting

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I've had a cough that won't stop for a few days.
lines.note: 며칠째 = for several days now; ~아서/어서요 trails off to give a reason

lines.ko: 알겠습니다. 저쪽에서 잠시만 기다려 주세요. 성함 부를게요.
lines.romanization: algetseumnida. jeojjogeseo jamsiman gidaryeo juseyo. seongham bureulgeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Got it. Please wait over there for a moment. I'll call your name.
lines.note: 성함 = honorific for 'name'; 부르다 = to call

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Okay, do I pay the consultation fee after I'm done?
lines.note: 진료비 = medical/consultation fee

lines.ko: 네, 진료 끝나고 여기서 수납하시면 돼요.
lines.romanization: ne, jillyo kkeunnago yeogiseo sunapasimyeon dwaeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, you can settle the payment here after your consultation.
lines.note: 수납하다 = to pay/settle the bill, common at clinic desks

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you. I'll wait.

dialogues.tip: First-time patients fill out a short 문진표 (medical questionnaire) and show ID (your 외국인등록증 works). If you're enrolled in 건강보험, clinic visits are cheap. You usually see the doctor first and pay (수납) at the desk on your way out, then take any 처방전 to a nearby pharmacy.

dialogues.title: Part-time job interview
dialogues.situation: You go to a cafe to interview for an 알바 (part-time job) after seeing a 'staff wanted' notice.

lines.speaker: 사장님
lines.en: Hello. Are you here for the part-time job interview?
lines.note: 면접 보다 = to have/do an interview. 알바 is the everyday short form of 아르바이트.

lines.speaker: 지원자
lines.en: Yes, that's right. I'm the one who called yesterday.
lines.note: 전화드리다 is the humble form of 전화하다, polite toward the boss.

lines.ko: 네, 여기 앉으세요. 혹시 카페에서 일해 본 적 있어요?
lines.romanization: ne, yeogi anjeuseyo. hoksi kapeeseo ilhae bon jeok isseoyo?
lines.speaker: 사장님
lines.en: Okay, please have a seat. Have you ever worked at a cafe before?
lines.note: -아/어 본 적 있다 = 'have you ever (done)?', asking about experience.

lines.ko: 네, 전에 다른 카페에서 6개월 정도 일했어요.
lines.romanization: ne, jeone dareun kapeeseo 6gaewol jeongdo ilhaesseoyo.
lines.speaker: 지원자
lines.en: Yes, I worked at another cafe for about 6 months before.
lines.note: 정도 = 'about/approximately', softens the number.

lines.speaker: 사장님
lines.en: That's good. Can you come in on weekends too?
lines.note: 나오다 here means 'to come in (to work)'. -ㄹ 수 있다 = can/be able to.

lines.ko: 네, 주말은 다 괜찮고, 평일은 저녁에만 가능해요.
lines.romanization: ne, jumareun da gwaenchanko, pyeongireun jeonyeogeman ganeunghaeyo.
lines.speaker: 지원자
lines.en: Yes, weekends are all fine, and weekdays I'm only available in the evening.
lines.note: -만 = 'only'. 가능하다 = to be possible/available.

lines.ko: 시급은 만 원이고, 4대 보험은 안 돼요. 괜찮아요?
lines.romanization: sigeubeun man wonigo, 4dae boheomeun an dwaeyo. gwaenchanayo?
lines.speaker: 사장님
lines.en: The hourly wage is 10,000 won, and there's no employment insurance package. Is that okay?
lines.note: 시급 = hourly wage. 4대 보험 = the four major insurances; small 알바 jobs often skip it.

lines.speaker: 지원자
lines.en: Yes, that's fine. When can I start working?
lines.note: -(으)면 되다 = 'it's enough to / I just need to (do)'; here, 'when should I start?'

lines.ko: 이번 주 토요일부터 나오면 돼요. 11시까지 오세요.
lines.romanization: ibeon ju toyoilbuteo naomyeon dwaeyo. 11sikkaji oseyo.
lines.speaker: 사장님
lines.en: You can start this Saturday. Please come by 11.
lines.note: -부터 = from (starting point). -까지 = by/until (time limit).

lines.speaker: 지원자
lines.en: Okay, understood. I'll see you on Saturday!
lines.note: 뵙겠습니다 = humble 'I will see you', polite and professional toward an employer.

dialogues.tip: Always confirm the 시급 (hourly wage), schedule, and start date out loud before you leave. For any 알바, you have the legal right to a written contract (근로계약서) and at least the minimum wage, so it's fine to ask 근로계약서 써요? if they don't mention it.

dialogues.title: Calling in sick to your manager
dialogues.situation: You wake up sick and have to phone your 점장 (store manager) to say you can't make your shift today.

lines.speaker: 점장
lines.en: Hello?
lines.note: 여보세요 is the standard way to answer the phone in Korean.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Manager, it's me, Minsu. Is it okay to talk right now?
lines.note: 통화 괜찮으세요? = 'Is it a good time to talk?', a polite phone opener.

lines.speaker: 점장
lines.en: Oh, Minsu. What's up?
lines.note: 무슨 일이에요? = 'What's the matter?' / 'What's going on?'

lines.ko: 제가 아침부터 몸이 너무 안 좋아서요. 열도 나고 계속 토해요.
lines.romanization: jega achimbuteo momi neomu an joaseoyo. yeoldo nago gyesok tohaeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I've been feeling really unwell since this morning. I have a fever and keep throwing up.
lines.note: 몸이 안 좋다 = 'to feel unwell'. -아/어서요 ends a sentence by giving a reason.

lines.ko: 아이고, 많이 아파요? 병원은 가 봤어요?
lines.romanization: aigo, mani apayo? byeongwoneun ga bwasseoyo?
lines.speaker: 점장
lines.en: Oh no, are you very sick? Have you been to the doctor?
lines.note: 아이고 is a sympathetic exclamation. 병원 가다 = 'to go to the hospital/clinic'.

lines.ko: 지금 가려고요. 죄송한데 오늘 출근 못 할 것 같아요.
lines.romanization: jigeum garyeogoyo. joesonghande oneul chulgeun mo tal geot gatayo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm about to go now. I'm sorry, but I don't think I can come in to work today.
lines.note: -(으)ㄹ 것 같다 = 'I think / it seems'; softens bad news. 출근하다 = to go to work.

lines.ko: 음... 그럼 어쩔 수 없죠. 오늘은 푹 쉬어요.
lines.romanization: eum... geureom eojjeol su eopsjyo. oneureun puk swieoyo.
lines.speaker: 점장
lines.en: Hmm... well, then it can't be helped. Get plenty of rest today.
lines.note: 어쩔 수 없다 = 'there's no choice / it can't be helped'. 푹 쉬다 = to rest well.

lines.ko: 정말 죄송해요. 혹시 대신 나올 사람 제가 알아볼까요?
lines.romanization: jeongmal joesonghaeyo. hoksi daesin naol saram jega arabolkkayo?
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm really sorry. Should I try to find someone to cover for me?
lines.note: 대신 = 'instead/in place of'. 알아보다 = to look into / find out. Offering to help shows responsibility.

lines.ko: 아니에요, 그건 내가 알아볼게요. 몸조리 잘하고요.
lines.romanization: anieyo, geugeon naega arabolgeyo. momjori jalhagoyo.
lines.speaker: 점장
lines.en: No, I'll take care of that. Just take good care of yourself.
lines.note: 몸조리 잘하다 = 'take good care of your health', a common get-well phrase.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Okay, thank you. I'll definitely come in tomorrow.
lines.note: 꼭 = 'for sure/definitely'. -(으)ㄹ게요 expresses a promise to the listener.

dialogues.tip: Call as early as possible and always offer a clear reason plus an apology. Saying 죄송한데... before the bad news and offering to help find a 대타 (a fill-in) makes a great impression. If you visited a clinic, you can ask for a 진료확인서 (proof of treatment) in case your manager wants it.

dialogues.title: Ordering delivery food by phone
dialogues.situation: You phone a fried-chicken place to order 배달 (delivery) to your apartment.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, this is Kyochon Chicken. May I take your order?
lines.note: 주문 도와드릴까요? = 'May I help you with your order?', a standard restaurant greeting.

lines.ko: 네, 배달 되죠? 후라이드 한 마리 주문하려고요.
lines.romanization: ne, baedal doejyo? huraideu han mari jumunharyeogoyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, you do delivery, right? I'd like to order one whole fried chicken.
lines.note: 배달 되죠? = 'you do delivery, right?'. 한 마리 = 'one (whole) chicken'; 마리 counts animals.

lines.ko: 네, 후라이드 한 마리요. 더 필요하신 거 있으세요?
lines.romanization: ne, huraideu han mariyo. deo piryohasin geo isseuseyo?
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, one fried chicken. Is there anything else you need?
lines.note: 필요하신 거 = honorific form of 필요한 거 ('thing you need'), polite to the customer.

lines.ko: 콜라 한 병이랑 무 추가해 주세요.
lines.romanization: kolla han byeongirang mu chugahae juseyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Please add one bottle of cola and some pickled radish.
lines.note: -(이)랑 = 'and' (casual). 추가하다 = to add (an item). 무 = the pickled radish that comes with chicken.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Okay. What's your address?
lines.note: 주소가 어떻게 되세요? = the polite, standard way to ask for someone's address.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It's Haengbok Apartment, Building 103, Unit 502.
lines.note: 동 = building number, 호 = unit number; this is the normal order for Korean apartment addresses.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Will you pay by card or by cash?
lines.note: 결제 = payment. -(으)로 하다 = 'to do/go with (a method)'. A/B 하시겠어요? offers two choices politely.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'll pay by card. How long will it take?
lines.note: 얼마나 걸려요? = 'how long does it take?', essential for asking about delivery time.

lines.ko: 한 사십 분 정도 걸려요. 배달비는 삼천 원이에요.
lines.romanization: han sasip bun jeongdo geollyeoyo. baedalbineun samcheon wonieyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It'll take about forty minutes. The delivery fee is 3,000 won.
lines.note: 한 + number = 'about/roughly'. 배달비 = delivery fee, almost always charged separately now.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Okay, got it. Please call me when you arrive.
lines.note: -(으)면 = 'when/if'. 전화 주세요 = 'please give me a call', common request for delivery.

dialogues.tip: Have your address ready in 동/호 (building/unit) form before you call, and listen for the 배달비 (delivery fee) and 최소주문금액 (minimum order amount). Many places now prefer app orders, so if phoning feels hard, 배달의민족 or 쿠팡이츠 lets you do the whole thing without speaking.

dialogues.title: Signing Up for a Phone Plan
dialogues.situation: You go to a 통신사 store to sign up for a SIM card and a monthly mobile plan.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Welcome. How can I help you?
lines.note: 무엇을 도와드릴까요 = standard 'how may I help you?' at a counter

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'd like to sign up for a new phone plan.
lines.note: 요금제 = rate plan; 가입하다 = to sign up/subscribe

lines.ko: 유심만 필요하세요, 아니면 새 폰도 사실 거예요?
lines.romanization: yusimman piryohaseyo, animyeon sae pondo sasil geoyeyo?
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Do you just need a SIM card, or are you buying a new phone too?
lines.note: 유심 = SIM card (from 'USIM'); 폰 = casual for 휴대폰

lines.ko: 폰은 있어서 유심이랑 요금제만 하면 돼요.
lines.romanization: poneun isseoseo yusimirang yogeumjeman hamyeon dwaeyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I have a phone, so I just need a SIM and a plan.
lines.note: -만 하면 돼요 = I only need to do ~; 있어서 = since I have it

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Do you have your ARC and a card to pay with?
lines.note: 외국인등록증 = Alien Registration Card, required to open a plan

lines.ko: 네, 여기 있어요. 데이터 많이 쓰는데 무제한 있어요?
lines.romanization: ne, yeogi isseoyo. deiteo mani sseuneunde mujehan isseoyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, here you go. I use a lot of data — is there an unlimited plan?
lines.note: 데이터 무제한 = unlimited data; 많이 쓰다 = to use a lot

lines.ko: 이 요금제가 월 사만오천 원에 데이터 무제한이에요.
lines.romanization: i yogeumjega wol samanocheon wone deiteo mujehanieyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: This plan is 45,000 won a month with unlimited data.
lines.note: 월 사만오천 원 = 45,000 won per month; 월 = monthly

lines.ko: 약정 있어요? 중간에 해지하면 위약금 나와요?
lines.romanization: yakjeong isseoyo? junggane haejihamyeon wiyakgeum nawayo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Is there a contract? If I cancel partway, is there a penalty?
lines.note: 약정 = contract commitment; 해지 = cancellation; 위약금 = early-termination penalty

lines.ko: 무약정으로 하시면 위약금 없어요. 대신 할인은 좀 적어요.
lines.romanization: muyakjeongeuro hasimyeon wiyakgeum eopseoyo. daesin harineun jom jeogeoyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: If you go with no contract, there's no penalty. But the discount is a bit smaller.
lines.note: 무약정 = no-contract; 대신 = but in exchange/instead

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'll go with no contract. Can it be activated right away?
lines.note: 개통 = activation (of a line); -(으)ㄹ게요 = I'll do ~ (deciding)

lines.ko: 네, 본인 인증만 하면 십 분 안에 개통돼요.
lines.romanization: ne, bonin injeungman hamyeon sip bun ane gaetongdwaeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, once we verify your identity, it's activated within ten minutes.
lines.note: 본인 인증 = identity verification; -안에 = within (a time)

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Great. I'll sign up for that one. Thank you.
lines.note: 그걸로 = with that one (그것으로 shortened)

dialogues.tip: You need your 외국인등록증 (ARC) and a payment method to open a phone line. Ask for 무약정 (no contract) if you might leave Korea soon, so you avoid a 위약금 (early-termination penalty). A 알뜰폰 (budget MVNO) plan is often much cheaper than the big three carriers.

dialogues.title: Reporting a Lost Phone and Calling for Help
dialogues.situation: You realize your phone is missing in a cafe, then witness someone collapse and have to call 119.

lines.ko: 저기요, 제가 여기 핸드폰을 두고 간 것 같아요.
lines.romanization: jeogiyo, jega yeogi haendeuponeul dugo gan geot gatayo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Excuse me, I think I left my phone here.
lines.note: 두고 가다 = to leave (something) behind; 저기요 = polite way to get attention

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: What color is it, by any chance? Where were you sitting?
lines.note: 앉으셨어요 = honorific past 'where did you sit'; 혹시 = by any chance

lines.ko: 검은색 폰이고, 저 창가 자리에 앉았어요.
lines.romanization: geomeunsaek ponigo, jeo changga jarie anjasseoyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It's a black phone, and I was sitting at that window seat.
lines.note: 창가 자리 = window seat; 검은색 = the color black

lines.ko: 아, 이거 맞으세요? 직원이 보관하고 있었어요.
lines.romanization: a, igeo majeuseyo? jigwoni bogwanhago isseosseoyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Ah, is this it? A staff member was keeping it for you.
lines.note: 보관하다 = to keep/store; 맞으세요 = is it correct/yours?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, that's it! Thank you so much. What a relief.
lines.note: 다행이에요 = 'what a relief', said when something turns out okay

lines.ko: 어, 잠깐만요… 저기 어떤 분이 갑자기 쓰러졌어요!
lines.romanization: eo, jamkkanmanyo… jeogi eotteon buni gapjagi sseureojyeosseoyo!
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Oh, wait a second… someone over there suddenly collapsed!
lines.note: 쓰러지다 = to collapse/fall down; 갑자기 = suddenly

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Really? Quick, call 119 to report it!
lines.note: 신고하다 = to report (to police/emergency); 119 is fire & ambulance

lines.speaker: 상담원
lines.en: Yes, this is 119. What's the situation?
lines.note: 상담원 = the dispatcher/operator; 어떤 상황이세요 = what's the situation?

lines.ko: 사람이 쓰러졌어요. 의식이 없는 것 같아요.
lines.romanization: sarami sseureojyeosseoyo. uisigi eopsneun geot gatayo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: A person collapsed. They seem to be unconscious.
lines.note: 의식이 없다 = to be unconscious; -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요 = it seems that ~

lines.ko: 지금 위치가 어디예요? 주소나 가게 이름 말씀해 주세요.
lines.romanization: jigeum wichiga eodiyeyo? jusona gage ireum malsseumhae juseyo.
lines.speaker: 상담원
lines.en: Where are you right now? Please tell me an address or the shop's name.
lines.note: 위치 = location; 주소나 = an address or ~ (~(이)나 lists options)

lines.ko: 강남역 2번 출구 앞 스타벅스예요. 빨리 와 주세요!
lines.romanization: gangnamyeok 2beon chulgu ap seutabeokseuyeyo. ppalli wa juseyo!
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It's the Starbucks in front of Gangnam Station Exit 2. Please come quickly!
lines.note: 출구 = exit; 빨리 와 주세요 = please come quickly

lines.ko: 구급차 보낼게요. 제가 안내할 테니까 끊지 마세요.
lines.romanization: gugeupcha bonaelgeyo. jega annaehal tenikka kkeunchi maseyo.
lines.speaker: 상담원
lines.en: I'll send an ambulance. I'll guide you, so don't hang up.
lines.note: 구급차 = ambulance; 끊지 마세요 = don't hang up; -(으)ㄹ 테니까 = since I will ~

dialogues.tip: For fire or a medical emergency call 119; for crime or a lost/stolen item call 112. Both have English help, but the fastest thing is to give your 위치 (location) — a nearby station exit, shop name, or landmark works. Stay on the line; the 상담원 (operator) will guide you, including CPR instructions.

dialogues.title: Ordering at a Cafe and the Buzzer
dialogues.situation: You order a coffee at a cafe counter and the staff hands you a vibrating pager (진동벨) to wait for it.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Welcome. I'll take your order.
lines.note: 주문 도와드릴게요 = 'I'll help you order', the standard counter greeting

lines.ko: 아이스 아메리카노 한 잔이요. 사이즈는 제일 큰 걸로 주세요.
lines.romanization: aiseu amerikano han janiyo. saijeuneun jeil keun geollo juseyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: One iced americano. Give me the largest size, please.
lines.note: 제일 큰 걸로 = 'the biggest one'; 걸로 (= 것으로) is how you choose an option

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Are you having it here?
lines.note: 드시고 가세요? = the polite 'for here?'; the to-go version is 가져가세요?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: No, to go.
lines.note: 포장이요 = 'to go / takeout', the quickest way to say it

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Do you have a coupon or points to collect?
lines.note: 적립 = earning/stacking points; cafes ask this almost every time

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: No, it's fine. I'll pay by card.

lines.ko: 네, 사천오백 원 결제됐습니다. 진동벨 드릴게요.
lines.romanization: ne, sacheonobaek won gyeoljedwaetseumnida. jindongbel deurilgeyo.
lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Okay, that's 4,500 won, paid. Here's your pager.
lines.note: 진동벨 = the vibrating pager that buzzes when your drink is ready

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: A pager? How does this work?
lines.note: 어떻게 하는 거예요? = 'how do I do this?', natural for asking how something works

lines.ko: 음료 나오면 진동벨이 울려요. 그때 여기로 가져오시면 돼요.
lines.romanization: eumnyo naomyeon jindongberi ullyeoyo. geuttae yeogiro gajyeoosimyeon dwaeyo.
lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: When your drink is ready, the pager will buzz. Just bring it back here then.
lines.note: 진동벨이 울리다 = the pager goes off; -(으)면 돼요 = 'you just have to ~'

lines.ko: 아, 그러면 진동벨 받고 자리에서 기다리면 되는 거죠?
lines.romanization: a, geureomyeon jindongbel batgo jarieseo gidarimyeon doeneun geojyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Ah, so I take the pager and just wait at my seat, right?
lines.note: -는 거죠? = checking your understanding, 'right?'

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Yes, that's right. It'll be ready soon.
lines.note: 금방 나와요 = 'it comes out quickly', reassuring you about the wait

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Got it. Thank you.

dialogues.tip: Most Korean cafes give you a 진동벨 (vibrating pager) instead of calling your name. Take it to your seat — when it buzzes and lights up, bring it back to the counter to pick up your drink. Don't walk out with it. For takeout just say 포장이요, and staff will almost always ask about 적립 (points), which you can wave off with 괜찮아요.

dialogues.title: Exchanging Clothes for a Different Size
dialogues.situation: You bought a shirt that's too small and go back to the shop to exchange it for a bigger size.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Excuse me, I bought this yesterday and I'd like to exchange it.
lines.note: 교환하려고요 = 'I'm planning to exchange'; -(으)려고요 states your intention

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, is there something wrong with it?
lines.note: 어디가 문제세요? = a soft 'what's the issue?'

lines.ko: 사이즈가 좀 작아서요. 한 치수 큰 걸로 바꾸고 싶어요.
lines.romanization: saijeuga jom jagaseoyo. han chisu keun geollo bakkugo sipeoyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It's a bit too small. I'd like to change it for one size bigger.
lines.note: 한 치수 큰 거 = 'one size up'; 치수 is the word for clothing size

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Did you bring the receipt by any chance?
lines.note: 영수증 = receipt; shops usually need it for exchanges

lines.ko: 네, 여기 있어요. 택도 안 뗐어요.
lines.romanization: ne, yeogi isseoyo. taekdo an ttesseoyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, here it is. I didn't take the tag off either.
lines.note: 택 = price/brand tag; 안 떼다 = to not remove it — keeping it is important for exchanges

lines.ko: 잘하셨어요. 잠시만요, 큰 사이즈 있는지 확인해 볼게요.
lines.romanization: jalhasyeosseoyo. jamsimanyo, keun saijeu inneunji hwaginhae bolgeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Good. One moment, let me check if we have it in a bigger size.
lines.note: 있는지 확인해 볼게요 = 'I'll check whether we have it'; -는지 = whether

lines.ko: 손님, 죄송한데 그 색은 큰 사이즈가 다 나갔어요.
lines.romanization: sonnim, joesonghande geu saegeun keun saijeuga da nagasseoyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Ma'am/Sir, I'm sorry, but that color is sold out in the larger size.
lines.note: 다 나갔어요 = 'it's all gone / sold out', very common in shops

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Then is it available in another color?

lines.ko: 네, 검은색은 큰 사이즈 있어요. 그걸로 교환해 드릴까요?
lines.romanization: ne, geomeunsaegeun keun saijeu isseoyo. geugeollo gyohwanhae deurilkkayo?
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, we have the black one in the larger size. Shall I exchange it for that?
lines.note: 교환해 드릴까요? = 'shall I exchange it for you?', polite offer

lines.ko: 네, 그걸로 할게요. 혹시 입어 봐도 돼요?
lines.romanization: ne, geugeollo halgeyo. hoksi ibeo bwado dwaeyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, I'll take that. Can I try it on, by the way?
lines.note: 입어 봐도 돼요? = 'may I try it on?'; -아/어 봐도 돼요 = may I try ~ing

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Of course, the fitting room is over there.
lines.note: 피팅룸 = fitting room; 저쪽 = over that way

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you. I'll go try it on.

dialogues.tip: For an exchange (교환) keep the 영수증 (receipt) and don't remove the 택 (tag) — most shops require both, and many won't take items back without them. Ask for 한 치수 크게/작게 (one size up/down). 교환 (swap) is usually easy; a 환불 (refund) to your card can be stricter, especially on sale items, so check the shop's policy.

dialogues.title: Booking a Restaurant Table by Phone
dialogues.situation: You call a restaurant to reserve a table for dinner on the weekend.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Hello, this is OO Restaurant. How can I help you?
lines.note: Shops answer the phone with 네, [가게 이름]입니다 = 'Yes, this is [shop name]'

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hi, I'm calling to make a reservation.
lines.note: 전화드렸어요 = humble 'I called'; -(으)려고 = in order to

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, for when would you like the reservation?
lines.note: 언제로 = for when; 예약해 드릴까요 = shall I book it for you?

lines.ko: 이번 주 토요일 저녁 일곱 시요.
lines.romanization: ibeon ju toyoil jeonyeok ilgop siyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: This Saturday at 7 p.m.
lines.note: 저녁 일곱 시 = 7 in the evening; trailing 요 makes a short answer polite

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: How many people?
lines.note: 분 = polite counter for people

lines.ko: 네 명이요. 혹시 창가 자리 돼요?
lines.romanization: ne myeongiyo. hoksi changga jari dwaeyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Four people. Could we possibly get a window seat?
lines.note: 혹시 = by any chance; 자리 돼요? = is a seat available?

lines.ko: 잠시만요… 네, 일곱 시에 창가 자리 가능해요.
lines.romanization: jamsimanyo… ne, ilgop sie changga jari ganeunghaeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: One moment… yes, a window seat is available at seven.
lines.note: 잠시만요 = just a moment; 가능해요 = it's possible/available

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Oh good. Then I'll take that.
lines.note: 다행이다 = 'what a relief', said to oneself; 그걸로 할게요 = I'll go with that

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Could you give me the name and phone number for the reservation?
lines.note: 예약자 성함 = name under the booking; 연락처 = contact number

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: The name is Kim Minsu, and the number is 010-1234-5678.
lines.note: Korean phone numbers start with 010; read digits one by one

lines.ko: 확인했습니다. 토요일 일곱 시, 네 분 예약됐어요.
lines.romanization: hwaginhaetseumnida. toyoil ilgop si, ne bun yeyakdwaesseoyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Confirmed. Your reservation is for Saturday at seven, four people.
lines.note: 예약됐어요 = it's been booked (passive of 예약하다)

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you. See you that day.
lines.note: 그날 뵐게요 = 'I'll see you that day' (뵙다 = humble 'to see/meet')

dialogues.tip: Popular restaurants fill up on weekends, so call ahead. Many places now take bookings through apps like 캐치테이블 (CatchTable) or 네이버 예약, but a quick phone call still works everywhere. If you can't make it, call to cancel — some places charge a 노쇼 (no-show) fee.

dialogues.title: Describing Your Symptoms to the Doctor
dialogues.situation: You see the doctor at a clinic and explain that you've had a fever, sore throat, and body aches.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Hello. What brings you in today?
lines.note: 어디가 불편해서 오셨어요? = the standard way a doctor asks what's wrong (불편하다 = to be uncomfortable)

lines.ko: 이틀 전부터 열이 나고 목이 너무 아파요.
lines.romanization: iteul jeonbuteo yeori nago mogi neomu apayo.
lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I've had a fever since two days ago and my throat hurts a lot.
lines.note: 이틀 전부터 = since two days ago; 열이 나다 = to run a fever

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Do you also have a cough or runny nose?
lines.note: 기침 = cough; 콧물 = runny nose; -(이)나 lists options

lines.ko: 기침이 좀 나고, 몸살도 있는 것 같아요.
lines.romanization: gichimi jom nago, momsaldo inneun geot gatayo.
lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I have a bit of a cough, and I think I have body aches too.
lines.note: 몸살 = body aches/fatigue from being sick; -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요 = it seems that ~

lines.ko: 한번 열 좀 재 볼게요. 입 벌리고 '아' 해 보세요.
lines.romanization: hanbeon yeol jom jae bolgeyo. ip beolligo 'a' hae boseyo.
lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Let me take your temperature. Open your mouth and say 'ah'.
lines.note: 열을 재다 = to take a temperature; 입 벌리다 = to open one's mouth

lines.ko: 아… 침 삼킬 때 목이 많이 따가워요.
lines.romanization: a… chim samkil ttae mogi mani ttagawoyo.
lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Ahh… my throat really stings when I swallow.
lines.note: 침 삼키다 = to swallow (saliva); 따갑다 = to sting/be sore

lines.ko: 목이 많이 부었네요. 독감 검사 한번 해 볼게요.
lines.romanization: mogi mani bueonneyo. dokgam geomsa hanbeon hae bolgeyo.
lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Your throat is quite swollen. Let's run a flu test.
lines.note: 붓다 = to swell (부었네요 = it's swollen); 독감 검사 = flu test

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Is it the flu? Will I get better soon if I take medicine?
lines.note: 낫다 = to get better (나아요 = irregular conjugation); 금방 = soon

lines.ko: 네, 약 잘 드시고 푹 쉬면 며칠 안에 나아요.
lines.romanization: ne, yak jal deusigo puk swimyeon myeochil ane naayo.
lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Yes, if you take your medicine and rest well, you'll recover within a few days.
lines.note: 푹 쉬다 = to rest well; 며칠 안에 = within a few days

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: How many days should I take off work?
lines.note: -는 게 좋을까요 = would it be good to ~? (asking for advice)

lines.ko: 이삼 일은 쉬세요. 처방전 드릴 테니까 근처 약국에서 약 받으세요.
lines.romanization: isam ireun swiseyo. cheobangjeon deuril tenikka geuncheo yakgugeseo yak badeuseyo.
lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Take two or three days off. I'll give you a prescription, so pick up the medicine at a nearby pharmacy.
lines.note: 이삼 일 = two or three days; 처방전 = prescription; 근처 약국 = nearby pharmacy

lines.ko: 네, 알겠습니다. 진단서도 한 장 부탁드려요.
lines.romanization: ne, algetseumnida. jindanseodo han jang butakdeuryeoyo.
lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Okay, got it. Please write me a medical certificate as well.
lines.note: 진단서 = doctor's note/medical certificate; 한 장 = one sheet; 부탁드려요 = I'd like to ask for ~

dialogues.tip: Tell the doctor when it started (이틀 전부터) and your main 증상 (symptoms) — 열이 나요, 목이 아파요, 기침이 나요. The doctor gives you a 처방전 (prescription), which you take to any nearby 약국. If you need time off work, ask for a 진단서 (medical certificate); some workplaces require one.

dialogues.title: Telling the Taxi Driver Where to Go and Asking the Fare
dialogues.situation: You flag down a taxi, give the driver your destination, and ask how much it will cost and how long it will take.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Welcome. Where shall I take you?
lines.note: 어디로 모실까요? = a polite 'where to?'; 모시다 is a humble verb drivers often use

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello. Please take me to Hongik University Station.
lines.note: -(으)로 가 주세요 = 'please go to ~'; -(으)로 marks the destination

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Hongik Univ. Station? Okay, got it. I'll get going.
lines.note: Drivers often repeat the destination back to confirm it

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How long does it take to get there?
lines.note: 얼마나 걸려요? = 'how long does it take?', for time or distance

lines.ko: 지금 길이 좀 막혀서 한 삼십 분 정도 걸릴 것 같아요.
lines.romanization: jigeum giri jom makyeoseo han samsip bun jeongdo geollil geot gatayo.
lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Traffic's a bit heavy right now, so it'll probably take about thirty minutes.
lines.note: 길이 막히다 = the road is jammed; 한 ~ 정도 = roughly about ~

lines.ko: 혹시 좀 빠른 길로 가 주실 수 있어요?
lines.romanization: hoksi jom ppareun gillo ga jusil su isseoyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Could you take a faster route, if possible?
lines.note: 빠른 길로 = by the quicker road; -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요? = is it possible to ~?

lines.ko: 그럼 큰길 말고 골목으로 갈게요. 그게 더 빨라요.
lines.romanization: geureom keungil malgo golmogeuro galgeyo. geuge deo ppallayo.
lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Then I'll take the side streets instead of the main road. That's faster.
lines.note: 큰길 = main road, 골목 = back alley/side street; A 말고 B = B instead of A

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Okay, thank you. Also, can I pay by card?
lines.note: 카드로 결제돼요? = 'does card payment work?'; almost all Korean taxis take cards

lines.ko: 그럼요, 카드 다 됩니다. 다 왔어요, 손님. 여기 세워 드릴게요.
lines.romanization: geureomyo, kadeu da doemnida. da wasseoyo, sonnim. yeogi sewo deurilgeyo.
lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Of course, all cards work. We're here. I'll pull over right here.
lines.note: 다 왔어요 = 'we've arrived'; 세워 드릴게요 = 'I'll stop (the car) for you'

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How much is the fare?
lines.note: 얼마 나왔어요? = 'how much did it come out to?', the natural way to ask a metered total

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: It comes to 11,500 won.
lines.note: 만 천오백 원 = 11,500 won; fares are read straight off the meter (미터기)

lines.ko: 여기 카드요. 감사합니다. 좋은 하루 보내세요.
lines.romanization: yeogi kadeuyo. gamsahamnida. joeun haru bonaeseyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Here's my card. Thank you. Have a good day.
lines.note: 좋은 하루 보내세요 = a friendly 'have a nice day' when getting out

dialogues.tip: These days most people call a taxi with the 카카오택시 app, but you can still flag one with an empty 빈차 light. Give the destination as 목적지 + -(으)로 가 주세요, and ask the meter total with 얼마 나왔어요?. Cards work in nearly every taxi, so 카드로 결제돼요? is enough. Late at night a 심야 할증 (late-night surcharge, usually after midnight) is added automatically, so don't be surprised if the meter starts higher.

dialogues.title: Asking for a Haircut and Style at a Hair Salon
dialogues.situation: You go to a hair salon (미용실) and explain to the stylist how you want your hair cut and styled.

lines.speaker: 디자이너
lines.en: Hello. What would you like done today?
lines.note: 어떻게 해 드릴까요? = 'how shall I do it for you?', the standard salon opener

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Just a cut, please. My hair's gotten too long.
lines.note: 커트 = (a) haircut; -만 하려고요 = 'I'm only going to do ~'

lines.ko: 어느 정도 자를까요? 많이 자를까요, 아니면 살짝 다듬을까요?
lines.romanization: eoneu jeongdo jareulkkayo? mani jareulkkayo, animyeon saljjak dadeumeulkkayo?
lines.speaker: 디자이너
lines.en: How much should I take off? A lot, or just a light trim?
lines.note: 자르다 = to cut; 다듬다 = to trim/tidy up the ends

lines.ko: 기장은 어깨 정도로 하고, 앞머리는 그대로 두고 싶어요.
lines.romanization: gijangeun eokkae jeongdoro hago, ammeorineun geudaero dugo sipeoyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'd like the length around shoulder-length, and please leave the bangs as they are.
lines.note: 기장 = (hair) length; 앞머리 = bangs/fringe; 그대로 두다 = to leave it as is

lines.ko: 숱은 좀 칠까요? 끝이 많이 상했네요.
lines.romanization: suteun jom chilkkayo? kkeuchi mani sanghaenneyo.
lines.speaker: 디자이너
lines.en: Shall I thin it out a bit? The ends are pretty damaged.
lines.note: 숱을 치다 = to thin out the volume; 상하다 = (hair) to be damaged

lines.ko: 네, 숱 좀 쳐 주시고 끝만 정리해 주세요.
lines.romanization: ne, sut jom chyeo jusigo kkeunman jeongnihae juseyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, thin it out a little and just clean up the ends.
lines.note: 정리하다 = to tidy/clean up; a soft way to ask for a neat finish

lines.ko: 혹시 펌이나 염색도 같이 하실 생각 있으세요?
lines.romanization: hoksi peomina yeomsaekdo gachi hasil saenggak isseuseyo?
lines.speaker: 디자이너
lines.en: By any chance, were you thinking of getting a perm or color done too?
lines.note: 펌 = perm, 염색 = hair dye/coloring; common add-on questions

lines.ko: 오늘은 커트만 할게요. 펌은 다음에 할까 봐요.
lines.romanization: oneureun keoteuman halgeyo. peomeun daeume halkka bwayo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Just the cut today. I'm thinking I'll do the perm next time.
lines.note: -(으)ㄹ까 봐요 here = 'I think I might ~'; a soft way to put something off

lines.ko: 네, 그럼 머리 먼저 감겨 드릴게요. 이쪽으로 오세요.
lines.romanization: ne, geureom meori meonjeo gamgyeo deurilgeyo. ijjogeuro oseyo.
lines.speaker: 디자이너
lines.en: Okay, then let me wash your hair first. Come this way.
lines.note: 머리를 감기다 = to wash someone's hair (for them); 감다 is to wash your own

lines.ko: 혹시 다 하면 시간 얼마나 걸려요?
lines.romanization: hoksi da hamyeon sigan eolmana geollyeoyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: About how long will the whole thing take?
lines.note: 다 하면 = 'once it's all done'; useful for planning your day

lines.ko: 커트만 하면 삼십 분이면 끝나요. 편하게 계세요.
lines.romanization: keoteuman hamyeon samsip bunimyeon kkeunnayo. pyeonhage gyeseyo.
lines.speaker: 디자이너
lines.en: Just a cut takes thirty minutes. Make yourself comfortable.
lines.note: -(으)면 끝나요 = 'it's done in ~'; 편하게 계세요 = 'relax / make yourself at home'

lines.ko: 감사합니다. 너무 짧지 않게만 해 주세요.
lines.romanization: gamsahamnida. neomu jjalbji ankeman hae juseyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you. Just please don't make it too short.
lines.note: 너무 짧지 않게 = 'not too short'; -지 않게 (해 주세요) = please make it not ~

dialogues.tip: At a 미용실 (hair salon) the cutter is called a 디자이너. The key words are 다듬다 (a light trim), 자르다 (a real cut), 기장 (length), 숱 (thickness/volume), 앞머리 (bangs), 펌 (perm), and 염색 (coloring). To be safe, say how much in concrete terms — 어깨 기장으로 (to shoulder length) or 손가락 두 마디 정도 (about two finger-joints) — and 너무 짧지 않게 해 주세요 if you're nervous. Bringing a photo and saying 이렇게 해 주세요 (please do it like this) works great.

dialogues.title: Making Weekend Plans with a Friend
dialogues.situation: You text and then call a close friend to figure out what to do this weekend.

lines.speaker: 지민
lines.en: Hey, what are you doing this weekend?
lines.note: 야 = casual 'hey' to a close friend; 뭐 해? drops the polite 요 for 반말

lines.ko: 아직 아무 계획 없는데. 왜, 뭐 하게?
lines.romanization: ajik amu gyehoek eopsneunde. wae, mwo hage?
lines.speaker: 친구
lines.en: I've got no plans yet. Why, what's up?
lines.note: -는데 softens the statement and invites a follow-up; 뭐 하게? = 'what, are you planning something?'

lines.speaker: 지민
lines.en: I'm just bored. Want to hang out Saturday?
lines.note: 놀다 = to hang out/play; -(으)ㄹ까? = 'shall we ~?' for suggestions

lines.speaker: 친구
lines.en: Sounds good! But did you decide what to do?
lines.note: 좋지! = 'sure, sounds great' (지 adds a friendly, agreeing tone); 뭐 할지 = what (we'll) do

lines.ko: 성수동 가서 카페 투어 어때? 요즘 핫하잖아.
lines.romanization: seongsudong gaseo kape tueo eottae? yojeum hatajana.
lines.speaker: 지민
lines.en: How about going to Seongsu and doing a cafe tour? It's super trendy these days.
lines.note: 핫하다 = 'to be hot/trendy' (borrowed slang); -잖아 = 'you know, right?' assuming shared knowledge

lines.ko: 오 좋아. 사진 찍기도 예쁘고. 몇 시에 만날까?
lines.romanization: o joa. sajin jjikgido yeppeugo. myeot sie mannalkka?
lines.speaker: 친구
lines.en: Oh nice. It's pretty for photos too. What time should we meet?
lines.note: 사진 찍기 = taking photos; 만날까? = 'shall we meet?'

lines.ko: 두 시쯤? 너무 이르면 사람 많아.
lines.romanization: du sijjeum? neomu ireumyeon saram mana.
lines.speaker: 지민
lines.en: Around 2-ish? If it's too early it gets crowded.
lines.note: -쯤 = 'around/about ~'; 이르다 = to be early

lines.speaker: 친구
lines.en: Deal. Then meet at Seongsu Station?
lines.note: 콜 = 'deal/I'm in', extremely common slang for agreeing to plans

lines.ko: 응, 2번 출구 앞에서 보자. 늦으면 카톡해.
lines.romanization: eung, 2beon chulgu apeseo boja. neujeumyeon katokae.
lines.speaker: 지민
lines.en: Yeah, let's meet in front of Exit 2. Text me if you're late.
lines.note: 출구 = subway exit; 카톡하다 = 'to KakaoTalk (someone)', used as a verb for messaging

lines.ko: 오케이. 아, 나 차 안 가져가니까 지하철로 갈게.
lines.romanization: okei. a, na cha an gajyeoganikka jihacheollo galge.
lines.speaker: 친구
lines.en: Okay. Oh, I'm not bringing my car, so I'll take the subway.
lines.note: 안 가져가다 = not bring/take (something); -(으)ㄹ게 = 'I'll ~' stating your own intention

lines.ko: 잘됐다. 끝나고 저녁도 먹자. 그날 봐!
lines.romanization: jaldwaetda. kkeunnago jeonyeokdo meokja. geunal bwa!
lines.speaker: 지민
lines.en: Perfect. Let's grab dinner after too. See you that day!
lines.note: 잘됐다 = 'great, that worked out'; 먹자 = 'let's eat' (-자 = casual 'let's')

lines.speaker: 친구
lines.en: OK, I'll get in touch later. See you then!
lines.note: ㅇㅋ = texting shorthand for 오케이; 연락하다 = to get in touch/contact

dialogues.tip: With close friends you drop the 요 and use 반말. To suggest plans, end with -(으)ㄹ까? ('shall we?') and to lock something in just say 콜 or 오케이. Almost everyone arranges meetups over 카톡 (KakaoTalk), and meeting spots are usually given as a subway exit number, like 2번 출구 앞 ('in front of Exit 2').

dialogues.title: Politely Asking a Neighbor About Noise
dialogues.situation: Late at night you knock on your upstairs neighbor's door to ask them to keep the floor noise down.

lines.speaker: 이웃
lines.en: Yes, who is it?
lines.note: Standard way to answer the door; 누구세요? = 'who is it?' (honorific 세)

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Hi, I'm the person living downstairs.
lines.note: 아래층 = the floor below; -는데요 softens the opening and signals more is coming

lines.speaker: 이웃
lines.en: Oh, yes. What's the matter?
lines.note: 무슨 일이세요? = 'what's going on / how can I help?' (polite)

lines.ko: 다름이 아니라, 밤에 층간소음 때문에 좀 힘들어서요.
lines.romanization: dareumi anira, bame cheunggansoeum ttaemune jom himdeureoseoyo.
lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: It's just that the noise between floors at night has been a bit tough.
lines.note: 다름이 아니라 = 'it's nothing major, but…', a polite way to raise an issue; 층간소음 = inter-floor noise

lines.speaker: 이웃
lines.en: Oh my, really? Was it loud? I didn't realize.
lines.note: 어머 = 'oh my' (mild surprise); -았나요? = a soft 'was it ~?' question

lines.ko: 밤 열한 시 넘어서 쿵쿵 소리가 나서요. 혹시 아기가 있어요?
lines.romanization: bam yeolhan si neomeoseo kungkung soriga naseoyo. hoksi agiga isseoyo?
lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: There's a thumping sound after 11 p.m. Do you by any chance have a little one?
lines.note: 쿵쿵 = thump-thump (onomatopoeia for heavy footsteps); 혹시 = 'by any chance' to ask gently; 아기 = baby

lines.ko: 네, 애들이 둘이에요. 뛰지 말라고 해도 잘 안 들어서…
lines.romanization: ne, aedeuri durieyo. ttwiji mallago haedo jal an deureoseo…
lines.speaker: 이웃
lines.en: Yes, I have two kids. Even when I tell them not to run, they don't really listen…
lines.note: 뛰다 = to run/jump; -지 말라고 하다 = to tell someone not to do something

lines.ko: 이해해요. 그래도 밤늦게만 좀 조심해 주시면 감사하겠습니다.
lines.romanization: ihaehaeyo. geuraedo bamneutgeman jom josimhae jusimyeon gamsahagetseumnida.
lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: I understand. Still, I'd be grateful if you could just be a little careful late at night.
lines.note: 밤늦게 = late at night (one word); 조심해 주시면 = 'if you would be careful' (the -아/어 주시다 form makes a polite request); 감사하겠습니다 = 'I would be thankful'

lines.ko: 당연하죠. 정말 죄송해요. 매트라도 깔아 볼게요.
lines.romanization: dangyeonhajyo. jeongmal joesonghaeyo. maeteurado kkara bolgeyo.
lines.speaker: 이웃
lines.en: Of course. I'm really sorry. I'll at least try putting down a mat.
lines.note: 당연하죠 = 'of course, naturally'; 매트라도 = 'a mat at least'; 깔다 = to lay down/spread

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Thank you. I'm sorry for being so sensitive too.
lines.note: 예민하다 = to be sensitive/touchy; -게 굴다 = to act/behave in a certain way

lines.speaker: 이웃
lines.en: Not at all. If anything bothers you, please tell me anytime.
lines.note: 언제든지 = anytime; 말씀하세요 = 'please tell me' (말씀 = honorific 'words/speech')

lines.ko: 네, 그럼 좋은 밤 되세요. 들어가세요.
lines.romanization: ne, geureom joeun bam doeseyo. deureogaseyo.
lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Okay, then have a good night. Go on in.
lines.note: 들어가세요 = 'please go in', a normal friendly closing when someone's at their door

dialogues.tip: 층간소음 (noise between floors) is one of the most common neighbor disputes in Korean apartments. Going up to complain in person can backfire, so many people first ask the building's 경비실 (security office) or 관리사무소 (management office) to pass on the message. If you do go yourself, stay in 요-form, open with 다름이 아니라…, and frame it as a request, not an accusation — it keeps the peace.

dialogues.title: Sending a Parcel at the Post Office
dialogues.situation: You go to the 우체국 to mail a box of clothes to a friend in another city and ask about price and delivery time.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Next, please. What would you like to send?
lines.note: 다음 분이요 = 'next person, please' (calling the next customer); 보내시겠어요? = honorific 'would you like to send?'

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'd like to send this parcel. To Busan.
lines.note: 택배 = parcel/courier delivery; -(으)려고요 = 'I'm planning to ~'; -(으)로 marks the destination

lines.ko: 안에 뭐 들었어요? 깨지는 물건 있어요?
lines.romanization: ane mwo deureosseoyo? kkaejineun mulgeon isseoyo?
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: What's inside? Anything breakable?
lines.note: 뭐 들었어요? = what's in it?; 깨지는 물건 = breakable item (깨지다 = to break)

lines.ko: 옷이랑 책 몇 권이요. 깨지는 건 없어요.
lines.romanization: osirang chaeng myeot gwoniyo. kkaejineun geon eopseoyo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Some clothes and a few books. Nothing breakable.
lines.note: -(이)랑 = and (casual); 몇 권 = a few (counter 권 for books)

lines.ko: 그럼 무게부터 잴게요. 여기 위에 올려 주세요.
lines.romanization: geureom mugebuteo jaelgeyo. yeogi wie ollyeo juseyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then let me weigh it first. Please put it up here.
lines.note: 무게를 재다 = to weigh; -부터 = starting with; 올리다 = to put up/place on

lines.ko: 얼마 나와요? 그리고 부산까지 며칠 걸려요?
lines.romanization: eolma nawayo? geurigo busankkaji myeochil geollyeoyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How much does it come to? And how many days to Busan?
lines.note: 얼마 나와요? = how much does it come out to?; 며칠 걸려요? = how many days does it take? (며칠, never 몇일)

lines.ko: 육천 원이고요, 일반으로 보내면 보통 이틀이면 도착해요. 더 빨리 받으시려면 익일특급도 있어요.
lines.romanization: yukcheon wonigoyo, ilbaneuro bonaemyeon botong iteurimyeon dochakaeyo. deo ppalli badeusiryeomyeon igilteukgeupdo isseoyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's 6,000 won, and with regular shipping it usually arrives in two days. If you want it sooner, there's next-day express too.
lines.note: -이고요 = 'it is ~, and' (polite linking); 일반 = regular; -(이)면 = if/when; 익일특급 = next-day express; -(으)려면 = if you want to ~

lines.ko: 그냥 일반으로 할게요. 송장은 어떻게 써요?
lines.romanization: geunyang ilbaneuro halgeyo. songjangeun eotteoke sseoyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'll just go with regular. How do I fill out the waybill?
lines.note: 일반 = regular (vs. express); 송장 = waybill/shipping label; -(으)ㄹ게요 = I'll ~ (deciding)

lines.ko: 여기 받는 분 성함하고 주소, 연락처 적어 주세요.
lines.romanization: yeogi banneun bun seonghamhago juso, yeollakcheo jeogeo juseyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Write the recipient's name, address, and phone number here.
lines.note: 받는 분 = the recipient; 성함 = honorific for name; 적다 = to write down

lines.ko: 다 썼어요. 나중에 어디까지 왔는지 조회돼요?
lines.romanization: da sseosseoyo. najunge eodikkaji wanneunji johoedwaeyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'm done writing. Can I track where it is later?
lines.note: 어디까지 왔는지 = how far it has come; 조회되다 = to be trackable / able to be looked up

lines.ko: 네, 이 운송장 번호로 인터넷에서 조회하시면 돼요.
lines.romanization: ne, i unsongjang beonhoro inteoneseseo johoehasimyeon dwaeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, you can track it online with this tracking number.
lines.note: 운송장 번호 = tracking number; -(으)로 = by means of; -(으)시면 돼요 = you just need to ~

dialogues.tip: Bring your own box if you can — the post office sells boxes (우체국 박스) but charges for them. Say 일반 (regular) for the standard rate or 익일특급 for next-day express. Always keep the 운송장 번호 (tracking number) so you can check delivery status on the 우체국택배 app or website. For breakable items, ask them to add 파손주의 (fragile) tape.

dialogues.title: Signing Up at the Gym
dialogues.situation: You visit a neighborhood 헬스장 to sign up and ask about membership length, the locker, and PT sessions.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Hello. Are you here to ask about signing up?
lines.note: 등록 = registration/sign-up; 상담 받다 = to get a consultation; -(으)러 오다 = to come in order to ~

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, I'd like to look into a gym membership.
lines.note: 헬스장 = gym (everyday word); 회원권 = membership; 알아보다 = to look into

lines.ko: 얼마나 다니실 생각이세요? 기간별로 가격이 달라요.
lines.romanization: eolmana danisil saenggagiseyo? giganbyeollo gagyeogi dallayo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: How long are you thinking of attending? The price varies by period.
lines.note: 다니다 = to attend/go regularly; 기간별로 = by period; 다르다 = to be different

lines.ko: 세 달 끊으면 한 달에 얼마예요?
lines.romanization: se dal kkeuneumyeon han dare eolmayeyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: If I sign up for three months, how much per month?
lines.note: 끊다 = to buy/sign up for (a pass); 한 달에 = per month

lines.ko: 세 달은 한 달에 오만 원이에요. 육 개월은 더 싸요.
lines.romanization: se dareun han dare oman wonieyo. yuk gaeworeun deo ssayo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Three months is 50,000 won a month. Six months is cheaper.
lines.note: 육 개월 = six months; 더 싸요 = it's cheaper (싸다 = to be cheap)

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Can I rent workout clothes and a towel too?
lines.note: 운동복 = workout clothes; 수건 = towel; 빌리다 = to borrow/rent; -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 = can

lines.ko: 운동복 대여는 한 달에 만 원 추가예요. 락커는 무료고요.
lines.romanization: undongbok daeyeoneun han dare man won chugayeyo. rakkeoneun muryogoyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Clothing rental is 10,000 won extra a month. The locker is free.
lines.note: 대여 = rental; 추가 = extra/additional; 락커 = locker; 무료 = free of charge

lines.ko: PT도 받고 싶은데, 한 번 받아 볼 수 있어요?
lines.romanization: PTdo batgo sipeunde, han beon bada bol su isseoyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'd also like to do PT — can I try one session?
lines.note: PT(피티) = personal training; 받다 = to receive (a session); -아/어 보다 = to try ~ing

lines.ko: 그럼 무료 체험 한 번 잡아 드릴게요. 결제는 카드로 하시겠어요?
lines.romanization: geureom muryo cheheom han beon jaba deurilgeyo. gyeoljeneun kadeuro hasigesseoyo?
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then I'll set up one free trial for you. Will you pay by card?
lines.note: 무료 체험 = free trial; 잡다 = to book/arrange (here 'set up'); 결제 = payment; -(으)시겠어요? = polite 'will you ~?'

lines.ko: 네, 카드요. 혹시 중간에 환불도 돼요?
lines.romanization: ne, kadeuyo. hoksi junggane hwanbuldo dwaeyo?
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, by card. By the way, can I get a refund partway through?
lines.note: 중간에 = in the middle/partway; 환불 = refund; -도 돼요? = is ~ also allowed?

lines.ko: 남은 기간만큼은 환불 가능해요. 여기 신청서 작성해 주세요.
lines.romanization: nameun giganmankeumeun hwanbul ganeunghaeyo. yeogi sincheongseo jakseonghae juseyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: You can be refunded for the remaining period. Please fill out this form here.
lines.note: 남은 기간만큼 = as much as the remaining period; 신청서 = application form; 작성하다 = to fill out

dialogues.tip: Longer plans (육 개월, 일 년) cut the monthly price a lot, but only commit long-term once you're sure you'll keep going. Ask about 운동복 대여 (clothing rental) and 락커 (locker) — some gyms include them, others charge extra. By law, gyms must refund the unused portion if you cancel, though they may deduct a small penalty, so keep your receipt and check the 환불 규정 (refund policy) before signing.

dialogues.title: Ordering at a cafe
dialogues.situation: You order a drink at a coffee shop counter.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Welcome. Would you like to order?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, one americano please.
lines.note: 한 잔 = one cup

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Hot one or cold one?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Iced please.
lines.note: 아이스 = iced

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: What size would you like?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I will go with the small one.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: For here or to go?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: To go. How much is it?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: It is four thousand five hundred won.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Here is my card. Thank you.

dialogues.tip: Cafes always ask 따뜻한 거 (hot) or 아이스 (iced), so decide before you reach the counter.

dialogues.title: Ordering and paying at a restaurant
dialogues.situation: You order food at a casual restaurant and pay at the end.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: How many people?
lines.note: 분 = polite counter

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Two people.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sit over here. And your order?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: One bibimbap and one kimchi stew please.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Is spicy food okay for you?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, it is fine. Some water too please.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, please wait a moment.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Excuse me, I will pay now.
lines.note: 저기요 = excuse me

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It is fifteen thousand won in total.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I will pay by card. Thank you for the meal.

dialogues.tip: Say 저기요 to call staff, and pay at the counter or table when you are ready, since tipping is not expected in Korea.

dialogues.title: Buying items at a convenience store
dialogues.situation: You buy a few items at a convenience store counter.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Welcome.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Two of these please.
lines.note: 개 = item counter

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Do you need a bag?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, one please.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: The bag is one hundred won.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That is fine. How much is it all together?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: It is three thousand two hundred won.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I will pay in cash.
lines.note: 현금 = cash

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Here is eight hundred won change.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Okay, thank you.

dialogues.tip: Plastic bags usually cost extra in Korea, so staff will ask 봉투 필요하세요 before charging you.

dialogues.title: Taking a Taxi
dialogues.situation: You get into a taxi and tell the driver where to go.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Where are you going?
lines.note: common driver greeting

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Please go to Seoul Station.
lines.note: 으로 marks destination

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Yes, understood.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How long does it take?

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: It takes about twenty minutes.
lines.note: 한 means about

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Please stop at that traffic light.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Here? Yes, we have arrived.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How much is it?

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: It is nine thousand won.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Here you go. Thank you.

dialogues.tip: Most Korean taxis take cards, so you can say 카드 돼요 to ask if card payment is okay.

dialogues.title: Asking Subway Directions
dialogues.situation: You ask a station worker how to reach your destination by subway.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Excuse me, may I ask something?
lines.note: polite opener

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, go ahead.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I want to go to Gangnam Station.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Take line two.
lines.note: 호선 means line number

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Do I have to transfer here?
lines.note: 갈아타다 to transfer

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: No, just keep going straight.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How many stops is it?
lines.note: 정거장 means stop

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It is five stops.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you. That helped a lot.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Go safely.
lines.note: warm closing

dialogues.tip: Look for the line color and number on signs, and follow the arrow to the platform for your direction.

dialogues.title: Asking for Directions
dialogues.situation: You stop someone on the street to find a nearby place.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Excuse me, let me ask for directions.
lines.note: polite street opener

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Yes, what are you looking for?

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Is there a pharmacy near here?
lines.note: 근처 means nearby

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Yes, it is next to that convenience store.
lines.note: 옆 means beside

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Is it far from here?

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: No, it is five minutes on foot.
lines.note: 걸어서 on foot

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Go straight and it is on the right?
lines.note: 오른쪽 means right

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Yes, that is right. You will see it soon.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Thank you so much.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: You are welcome.
lines.note: polite reply

dialogues.tip: Koreans often point with an open hand rather than one finger, so watch their gesture for the direction.

dialogues.title: Buying Clothes
dialogues.situation: You are shopping for a shirt and need a different size.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Welcome. What are you looking for?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Please show me this shirt.
lines.note: 보여 주세요 = please show

lines.ko: 네, 여기 있어요. 한번 입어 보세요.
lines.romanization: ne, yeogi isseoyo. hanbeon ibeo boseyo.
lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Sure, here it is. Try it on.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It is a little small. Do you have a bigger one?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: What size are you?
lines.note: polite size question

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I am not sure. I usually wear large.

lines.ko: 그럼 이 라지 사이즈 입어 보세요.
lines.romanization: geureom i raji saijeu ibeo boseyo.
lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Then try on this large size.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It fits perfectly. How much is this?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: It is 35,000 won.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I will take this. Do you take card?

dialogues.tip: Most Korean shops let you try clothes on, and politely asking before trying something on is always appreciated.

dialogues.title: At the Pharmacy
dialogues.situation: You feel sick and describe your symptoms to a pharmacist.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Where does it hurt?
lines.note: common pharmacy opener

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Since yesterday I have a headache and a fever.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Do you have a cough too?

lines.ko: 네, 기침이 조금 나고 목도 아파요.
lines.romanization: ne, gichimi jogeum nago mokdo apayo.
lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, I cough a little and my throat hurts.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It seems like a cold. Take this medicine.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How many times a day do I take it?

lines.ko: 식사 후에 하루 세 번 드세요.
lines.romanization: siksa hue haru se beon deuseyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Take it three times a day after meals.
lines.note: 식사 후 = after meals

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Does this medicine make me sleepy?

lines.ko: 조금 졸릴 수 있어요. 운전하지 마세요.
lines.romanization: jogeum jollil su isseoyo. unjeonhaji maseyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It may make you a bit sleepy. Do not drive.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Got it. Thank you.

dialogues.tip: In Korea you can buy mild cold medicine at a pharmacy without a prescription, so just describe your symptoms clearly.

dialogues.title: Seeing a Doctor
dialogues.situation: You visit a clinic and explain your symptoms to the doctor.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: What brings you in?
lines.note: asks reason for visit

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: My stomach hurts a lot.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Since when has it hurt?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It has hurt since last night and I have diarrhea.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: What did you eat yesterday?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I ate raw fish. After that it started to hurt.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Lie down here and let me check.
lines.note: 누워서 = lie down and

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Is it very bad?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It is not serious. I will prescribe medicine.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Okay, thank you. Goodbye.

dialogues.tip: At a clinic the doctor usually gives you a prescription, which you then take to a nearby pharmacy to fill.

dialogues.title: Checking into a hotel
dialogues.situation: You arrive at a hotel front desk to check in for your stay.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello. I would like to check in.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, do you have a reservation?
lines.note: polite past form

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, I booked online.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: What is your name?
lines.note: honorific for name

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It is Kim Minsu. I booked two nights.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Please show me your passport.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Here it is. Is breakfast included too?

lines.ko: 네, 칠 층 식당에서 드시면 돼요.
lines.romanization: ne, chil cheung sikdangeseo deusimyeon dwaeyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, you can eat at the restaurant on the seventh floor.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you. What is the room number?

lines.ko: 삼백오 호예요. 카드 키 여기 있어요.
lines.romanization: sambaego hoyeyo. kadeu ki yeogi isseoyo.
lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It is room 305. Here is your card key.

dialogues.tip: Korean hotels usually ask for your passport at check-in, so keep it handy.

dialogues.title: Meeting someone new
dialogues.situation: You meet a new coworker for the first time and introduce yourself.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Hello. Nice to meet you.
lines.note: set first-meeting phrase

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Hello. Glad to meet you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: I am Sarah. I came from America.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Oh, really? I am Jihun.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Nice to meet you. What work do you do?

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: I am a designer. How about you, Sarah?
lines.note: 씨 = polite title

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: I am an English teacher.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Wow, that is cool. You speak Korean well.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Not at all. I still speak only a little.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: I look forward to working with you.
lines.note: common closing phrase

dialogues.tip: Koreans add the title 씨 after a given name to be polite, but never use it for yourself.

dialogues.title: A short call to a friend
dialogues.situation: You call a friend to make plans to meet later today.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Hello? Jimin, it is me.
lines.note: 여보세요 = phone hello

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Oh, hi! What are you doing now?
lines.note: casual speech

lines.ko: 그냥 집에 있어. 오늘 시간 있어?
lines.romanization: geunyang jibe isseo. oneul sigan isseo?
lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Just staying home. Do you have time today?

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Yeah, the evening is fine. Why?

lines.ko: 같이 영화 볼래? 새 영화 나왔어.
lines.romanization: gachi yeonghwa bollae? sae yeonghwa nawasseo.
lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Want to watch a movie together? A new one came out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Sounds good! What time should we meet?

lines.ko: 여섯 시 어때? 역 앞에서 보자.
lines.romanization: yeoseot si eottae? yeok apeseo boja.
lines.speaker: A
lines.en: How about six? Let us meet in front of the station.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Got it. See you later then.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Okay, do not be late. I will hang up!

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Okay, see you later. Bye!

dialogues.tip: Always answer the phone in Korean with 여보세요, even if you already know who is calling.
